Comments: No evidence of electoral register integration with the X-Road platform or other data exchange systems in Djibouti.

revision_notes: The cited World Bank Systematic Country Diagnostic does not address electoral integration specifically. A search of ANSIE's (the national X-Road data exchange operator) published flagship projects, e-Governance Academy project documentation on the X-Road rollout, and the ACE Electoral Knowledge Network found no mention of the electoral register being connected to Djibouti's data exchange platform. Score of 0 (Unknown/n.a.) confirmed — this reflects an absence of any public documentation of integration, not a confirmed finding of non-integration.
revised_comments: There is no publicly documented evidence that Djibouti's electoral register is connected to the ANSIE-operated X-Road data exchange platform. ANSIE's listed flagship projects (e-Services, SIGED, Interoperability, CERT, Réseau Intégré de l'État) make no reference to the electoral commission (CENI) or voter registration data, and no independent source describes such an integration.

Definition: Integration of driver's license registration and traffic offence data
Comments: No evidence of driver licensing integration with the X-Road data exchange platform in Djibouti.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Driver's licence and vehicle registration records held by the Direction des Mines et de la Sécurité Routière (Ministry of Interior) have been digitised, but a February 2026 ministry statement launching the national Mobile ID project explicitly describes current government digital initiatives, including driving licences, as fragmented owing to the absence of a unified, interoperable identity/data-sharing mechanism; linking licence data to the digital ID/interoperability layer is presented only as a future possibility. This is positive evidence of a confirmed non-integrated status rather than a genuine unknown, so the code is revised from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated).
revised_comments: Djibouti's driver's licence and vehicle registration records, held by the Direction des Mines et de la Sécurité Routière, are digitised but operate as a standalone system. The Ministry of Interior's February 2026 Mobile ID launch statement describes government digital initiatives, including driving licences, as fragmented, and presents future linkage of licence data to the national digital identity system as an aspiration rather than a committed integration. Driver licensing data is accordingly not yet integrated into the national data exchange platform.

Definition: Integration of statistics, census data, administrative data for planning, M&E, and evidence-based policymaking
Comments: No documented integration of statistics or national planning data with X-Road. The World Bank Systematic Country Diagnostic supports data development. Open data initiative is mentioned as a goal in the Digital Transformation Strategy.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Found a 2022 partnership agreement between Djibouti's National Statistics Institute (INSTAD) and the Djibouti Port Community System (DPCS) for real-time data exchange to strengthen national accounts and external-trade statistics, plus an active World Bank-funded statistics modernisation programme (additional financing approved March 2024) and a digitised 2024 population census (RGPH-3). These confirm genuine administrative-data exchange activity involving INSTAD, but none of the sources establish that this is integrated with the central government X-Road/ANSIE data exchange platform that this variable specifically concerns — DPCS is a separate sectoral (trade/logistics) platform. The evidence is real but its relevance to the variable's precise scope is uncertain, so this is flagged for human review rather than asserting a score change; the original 0 (Unknown) is left in place pending review.
revised_comments: Djibouti's National Institute of Statistics (INSTAD) has an active 2022 partnership with the Djibouti Port Community System (DPCS) for real-time exchange of trade and logistics data to strengthen national accounts and external-trade statistics, and is the beneficiary of a World Bank-funded statistics modernisation programme supporting the 2024 population and economic censuses. It is not established whether these arrangements extend to the central government data exchange (X-Road) platform operated by ANSIE.

Comments: Open data initiative is part of the Digital Transformation Strategy goals. E-Government portal provides citizen access to some information. revision_notes: Confirmed with the 2025 Freedom House Freedom in the World report (Djibouti's overall score unchanged at 24/100, 'Not Free'; the specific 'government operates with openness and transparency' indicator scores 0/4). No public dashboard or operations report for the ANSIE/X-Road data exchange was found; the Digital Transformation Strategy's open-data commitments remain largely aspirational, while the e-government portal and social media provide some limited citizen-facing disclosure. Score of 2 (Low – Limited Disclosure) confirmed; the Value Name wording differs cosmetically from the scale label but is not a substantive error. Year updated to 2025 to reflect the latest Freedom House data.
revised_comments: Public transparency around Djibouti's data exchange operations remains limited. There is no public dashboard, annual report, or published data-sharing register for the ANSIE-operated X-Road platform. Some general disclosure occurs through the e-government portal and social media, and the Digital Transformation Strategy references open data as a future goal, but Freedom House's 2025 assessment rates the government's overall openness and transparency at the lowest possible level (0/4), with an overall Freedom in the World score of 24/100.
